rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the search needs a cheap, simple baseline to calibrate performance and reduce uncertainty. config_001 tests whether a basic RNA-only, single-profile PCA representation provides a usable validation accuracy/F1 anchor. This will help later isolate the effects of multiprofile settings, aggregation, learned RNA encoders, image modality, and fusion before adding complexity.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline with moderate accuracy, leaving uncertainty about whether multiprofile aggregation can improve performance without adding modality or encoder complexity. config_002 tests this directly by keeping model setting and RNA encoder fixed while changing single-profile to multiprofile with a simple avgpool aggregation. This is the best next use of budget because it provides a controlled comparison to config_001, isolates the profile/aggregation effect, and avoids prematurely changing multiple factors such as modality, encoder, or fusion.

The main evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with avgpool substantially outperforms singleprofile RNA using the same PCA encoder, suggesting profile aggregation is important. config_003 tests whether transformer aggregation improves on avgpool while keeping model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed, directly isolating the aggregation choice. This is the best next experiment because it extends the currently strongest direction with a minimal, high-information comparison before moving to image or multimodal settings.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA substantially outperforms single-profile PCA and multiprofile transformer aggregation. The key remaining uncertainty within this promising setting is whether a learned RNA encoder can improve over PCA. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to SCVI while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, so it isolates the effect of RNA representation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best design, avoids introducing image or fusion confounds, and will clarify whether RNA encoder choice is an important factor before testing more complex multimodal configurations.

RNA-only results show multiprofile avgpool helps PCA (0.591 vs 0.485) and scvi_n200 multiprofile avgpool is best (0.650), but it is unclear whether the gain is due to the scvi encoder or to multiprofile/aggregation. config_004 tests scvi_n200 with singleprofile, the missing factorial point that changes only the encoder relative to config_001 and only profile/aggregation relative to config_005. This is the best next budget use because it isolates representation from profile setting, reduces uncertainty before testing more complex multimodal or aggregation variants, and may reveal a simpler strong RNA baseline.

The completed runs only cover RNA-only models, with config_005 showing that multiprofile avgpool plus scvi is the strongest RNA direction, but there is still no evidence on whether image features provide standalone signal. config_010 tests a simple image-only resnet50 single-profile baseline, isolating the image modality/encoder before adding profile, aggregation, or fusion complexity. This is the best next budget use because it reduces high uncertainty about a top-level design decision and will determine whether image-only or multimodal extensions are worth pursuing.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool, especially scvi_n200 (0.650 acc / 0.628 F1), which outperforms PCA and single-profile settings. The main remaining uncertainty within this promising branch is whether the untested scgpt encoder can improve on scvi_n200 while keeping profile and aggregation fixed. config_008 tests exactly that one-factor representation change, so it can identify the best RNA representation before adding image/fusion complexity and is a high-value exploitation step under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence is that scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool is the best completed configuration (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1), and multiprofile plus avgpool has also helped the PCA baseline. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool for this best RNA representation. config_006 changes only aggregation relative to the current best, so it isolates the aggregation effect while exploiting the most promising direction. This is an efficient next experiment because it may either find a better configuration or confirm that avgpool is the preferred aggregation for scvi, which will inform later multimodal/fusion choices.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 is strongest (accuracy ~0.65, F1 ~0.63), while image-only ResNet50 singleprofile is weak (accuracy 0.208, F1 0.172), leaving it unclear whether image features are useful at all or whether multiprofile aggregation can improve them. This experiment tests image-only multiprofile ResNet50 with avgpool, the aggregation that already works well for RNA, to isolate whether profile/aggregation improves the image modality before adding fusion. It is the best next budget use because it is a minimal extension of the only image baseline, avoids confounding fusion and RNA-encoder choices, and will clarify whether multimodal experiments with ResNet50 are worth pursuing or whether a different image encoder should be tested.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only scvi multiprofile is the strongest direction, with validation accuracy around 0.65 and F1 around 0.63, while image-only ResNet50 is weak, reaching only about 0.33 accuracy with multiprofile avgpool. The key uncertainty is whether a stronger image representation, ImageNet ViT-L, contains useful signal before spending budget on multimodal fusion. config_014 keeps profile=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool, matching the completed image ResNet50 multiprofile avgpool experiment, so it cleanly isolates the effect of image encoder representation. This is the best next experiment because it is informative even if its immediate accuracy may be lower than the current RNA-only best: if ViT-L alone improves substantially, a multimodal scvi+ViT extension becomes well justified; if it remains weak, multimodal experiments relying on poor image features are less attractive.
